candidate_policy: Prefer P0 planned rows with source_refs, write_scope, test_commands, acceptance, and done_signal.
Do not assign umbrella rows until a planner splits them.
Every implementation row starts with a failing test or fixture update.
Update progress.json and parity docs in the same slice that changes behavior.

phase-0-parser-adaptive.name: Phase 0 - Parser and adaptive selection foundation

items.name: Parse static HTML into queryable documents
items.contract: Parse HTML into a Document that preserves URL/domain metadata and supports CSS selection.
ready_when: A local HTML fixture can be parsed without network access.
acceptance: Document.CSS returns matching elements and Element exposes tag, text, and attributes.
done_signal: TestParseSelectsElementsWithCSS passes.

items.name: Selector pseudo-elements, extraction helpers, and custom types
items.contract: Port Scrapling selector extraction ergonomics: ::text, ::attr(name), get/getall, regex extraction, JSON parsing, TextHandler/TextHandlers, and AttributesHandler behavior.
ready_when: Basic CSS selection and Response selector behavior are validated.
acceptance: String fixtures prove ::text, ::attr, get/getall, regex extraction, JSON parsing, TextHandler/TextHandlers helpers, AttributesHandler behavior, and invalid pseudo-element errors.
done_signal: TestSelectorExtractionHelpers passes.

items.name: XPath selection and CSS-to-XPath translator parity
items.contract: Add XPath selection and the CSS-to-XPath translation behavior needed for Scrapling-compatible selector queries.
ready_when: Static document parsing and selector extraction helpers are stable.
acceptance: Fixtures prove Document, Response, Element, and Selection XPath queries, relative XPath, text and attribute XPath extraction, scoped CSS translation, and CSS ::text/::attr pseudo-element translation without network access.
done_signal: TestXPathAndTranslator passes.

items.name: Traversal, filtering, and text search helpers
items.contract: Port selector navigation and search helpers including parent, children, siblings, next/previous, ancestors, search/filter, find_by_text, find_by_regex, and find_similar.
ready_when: Selector extraction helpers are stable enough to express expected results.
acceptance: Local DOM fixtures prove parent, children, siblings, next/previous, ancestors, selection filter/search, direct-text lookup, regex lookup, scoped element lookup, and similar-element behavior.
done_signal: TestSelectorNavigationAndSearch passes.

items.name: Selector generation helpers
items.contract: Generate robust CSS, full CSS, XPath, and full XPath selectors for selected elements using a Go-native equivalent of Scrapling selector generation.
ready_when: Traversal helpers expose enough DOM context to generate selectors.
acceptance: Fixtures prove generated short and full CSS/XPath selectors anchor at id-bearing ancestors, use deterministic nth-of-type sibling indexes, and re-select the original element.
done_signal: TestSelectorGeneration and the full Go test suite pass.

items.name: Save adaptive fingerprints by domain and identifier
items.contract: Persist enough element identity to relocate the same logical element after markup changes while isolating records by domain.
ready_when: An element has been selected from a parsed document.
acceptance: Saved fingerprints are retrievable by domain and identifier.
The default domain path is deterministic when URL metadata is missing.
done_signal: Store tests pass without shared global state.

items.name: Relocate adaptive elements with deterministic scoring
items.contract: Score candidate elements from a changed document and return the best confident match without fabricating low-confidence matches.
ready_when: A fingerprint exists for the current domain and identifier.
acceptance: Relocation handles ID changes, wrapper insertion, no-match cases, best-candidate selection, and tie order.
done_signal: Relocation tests pass and low-confidence candidates return no match.

items.name: CSS adaptive selector fallback and auto-save modes
items.contract: Port the CSS half of Scrapling adaptive selector ergonomics: auto_save on CSS queries, selector-as-default adaptive keys, adaptive lookup by identifier, retrieve helper, percentage threshold, combined-selector key splitting, and adaptive_domain override.
ready_when: Save and relocate adaptive rows are validated.
acceptance: Fixtures prove Document.SelectCSS auto-save, selector-as-default keys, explicit identifiers, combined-selector key splitting, adaptive fallback, manual retrieve, threshold control, and domain override behavior.
done_signal: CSS adaptive selector mode tests pass.

items.name: Adaptive fingerprint parity review and diagnostics
items.contract: Compare Go fingerprints/scoring with upstream adaptive behavior and expose diagnostics for missed or low-confidence relocations.
ready_when: Relocation is deterministic and file storage is validated.
acceptance: Fixtures cover score explanations, threshold failures, upstream fingerprint fields including children, and diagnostic failure reasons.
done_signal: TestAdaptiveDiagnostics passes.

phase-1-response-fetcher.name: Phase 1 - Response and static fetcher parity

items.name: Response metadata and selector contract
items.contract: Expose a Response that carries URL, status code, headers, final body URL, request metadata, and selector behavior over the parsed document.
ready_when: A local response fixture can be constructed without network access.
not_ready_when: The row tries to implement JSON helpers, body decoding, or HTTP fetching in the same slice.
acceptance: A local fixture can build a Response, inspect URL/status/headers, and query it with CSS.
done_signal: Response metadata and selector contract test passes.

items.name: Response body, text, bytes, and JSON helpers
items.contract: Expose body bytes, decoded text, and JSON decoding helpers on Response without hiding parse or decode errors.
ready_when: Response metadata and selector contract is complete.
not_ready_when: The row tries to add HTTP fetching or session behavior.
acceptance: Response exposes immutable body bytes, decoded text, and typed JSON decoding with visible errors for invalid JSON.
done_signal: Response body helper tests pass.

items.name: Response cookies, history, meta, and captured XHR fields
items.contract: Extend Response parity with response cookies, redirect history, metadata, request/response header detail, encoding, and captured XHR attachment points.
ready_when: Response metadata/body rows and redirect taxonomy are complete.
acceptance: httptest and constructed fixtures prove cookies, history, meta merging, encoding, and captured XHR storage without live browser dependencies.
done_signal: TestResponseExtendedMetadata passes.

items.name: Static Fetcher method surface over net/http
items.contract: Provide static GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE methods over net/http that return Response values from local HTTP fixtures.
ready_when: Response metadata and body helper rows are complete.
not_ready_when: The row tries to include FetcherSession, proxy rotation, browser impersonation, or retry taxonomy.
acceptance: httptest fixtures prove GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, custom headers, request body handling, status codes, and response parsing.
done_signal: Static fetcher method tests pass without live network calls.

items.name: FetcherSession option merging and cookies
items.contract: Provide a FetcherSession that merges session defaults with per-request options while preserving cookies across requests.
ready_when: Static Fetcher method surface over net/http is complete.
not_ready_when: The row tries to add proxy rotation, browser impersonation, or retry taxonomy.
acceptance: httptest fixtures prove default headers, per-request overrides, cookies, and connection reuse through one session object.
done_signal: FetcherSession option merging and cookie tests pass.

items.name: Redirect, timeout, retry, and error taxonomy
items.contract: Classify static fetcher redirects, timeouts, retries, and blocked unsafe redirects with deterministic error values.
ready_when: FetcherSession option merging and cookies is complete.
not_ready_when: The row tries to add proxy rotation or TLS/browser impersonation.
acceptance: httptest fixtures prove safe redirects, disabled redirects, timeout errors, retry counts, and blocked private-address redirects.
done_signal: Redirect, timeout, retry, and error taxonomy tests pass.

items.name: Static request options: params, forms, JSON, auth, verify, and cookies
items.contract: Complete static fetcher request option parity for query params, form data, JSON bodies, basic auth, certificate verification flag, request cookies, and response cookie access.
ready_when: Static Fetcher methods and Response extended metadata are stable.
acceptance: httptest fixtures prove Params query merging, Data form encoding, JSON marshaling and default content type, BasicAuth, Verify=false TLS behavior, request cookies, explicit header precedence, body option conflicts, JSON marshal errors, and response cookie visibility.
done_signal: TestStaticFetcherRequestOptions passes.

items.name: Static proxy support and proxy error classification
items.contract: Add explicit per-request and per-session proxy configuration with visible proxy error classification before rotation is introduced.
ready_when: Fetcher error taxonomy is validated.
acceptance: Local proxy fixtures prove per-request proxy routing, proxy auth, per-session proxy defaults, per-request proxy override, scheme-specific proxy maps, invalid proxy option errors, response proxy metadata, and operator-visible proxy error kinds.
done_signal: TestStaticFetcherProxySupport passes.

items.name: Proxy rotator strategies
items.contract: Port ProxyRotator behavior with cyclic rotation, custom strategy hooks, string/dictionary-style configuration mapping, and proxy-error retry integration.
ready_when: Static proxy support is complete.
acceptance: Unit fixtures prove cyclic rotation, custom strategy hooks, empty/invalid proxy rejection, string and dictionary-style proxy config parsing, session-level rotated proxies, static proxy conflict rejection, and retry-on-proxy-error using the next rotated proxy.
done_signal: TestProxyRotator and the full Go test suite pass.

items.name: Static browser impersonation, HTTP/3, and stealthy headers boundary
items.contract: Evaluate and implement the Go-native boundary for Scrapling static fetcher impersonation claims, including browser-like headers, TLS/browser impersonation, and HTTP/3 where supported.
ready_when: Core static options and proxy support are complete.
acceptance: Fixtures prove explicit browser-like header generation without overwriting caller headers and unsupported impersonation/HTTP3 modes return honest operator-visible errors before sending a request.
done_signal: TestStaticFetcherIdentityOptions and the full Go test suite pass; boundaries document supported claims.

items.name: Fetch safety controls: robots and private network blocking
items.contract: Add explicit operator-visible fetch safety controls for robots.txt enforcement and private-network/CIDR blocking across static fetch paths, with browser fetch integration planned as a follow-up rather than an implicit side effect.
ready_when: Static fetcher request options and error taxonomy are validated.
Hermetic httptest fixtures can serve target pages and robots.txt responses.
not_ready_when: The row attempts crawler politeness, rate limiting, or browser resource interception beyond robots and private network blocking.
The row requires live DNS, live web access, or privileged network configuration.
acceptance: httptest fixtures prove robots.txt allow and disallow decisions without live network access.
Pre-dispatch fixtures prove private IPv4, IPv6, localhost, and configured CIDR targets are rejected before request dispatch when blocking is enabled.
Safety decisions return typed/operator-visible FetcherError values and remain opt-in request options.
done_signal: TestFetcherSafetyControls, TestRobotsRuleSpecificity, and TestParseSafetyCIDRsRejectsInvalidCIDR pass.
boundaries.md documents opt-in robots/private-network safety controls and the separate browser integration boundary.

items.name: Async and concurrent static fetcher API
items.contract: Provide a Go-native concurrent equivalent for Scrapling AsyncFetcher and async sessions using context, goroutines, cancellation, and bounded concurrency.
ready_when: Static fetcher options are stable.
not_ready_when: The row tries to mimic Python awaitable syntax instead of exposing a Go-native context and result API.
The row requires live web access or background goroutines after Fetch returns.
acceptance: httptest fixtures prove bounded concurrent fetches return results in input order while overlapping request execution.
Context cancellation is propagated to in-flight requests and queued work without leaving background goroutines.
Per-request errors are collected beside successful responses, and a shared FetcherSession can supply cookies/defaults to concurrent calls without Python-style async mimicry.
done_signal: TestConcurrentFetcher and the full Go test suite pass; generated queue docs expose the next assignable row.

items.name: File-backed adaptive store with compatibility migration
items.contract: Persist adaptive fingerprints beyond process memory with explicit schema versioning and deterministic migration tests.
ready_when: The in-memory store contract remains stable after response/fetcher design.
acceptance: A file-backed store can save, reload, isolate domains, and reject incompatible schema versions visibly.
done_signal: File store tests pass with temp directories only.

items.name: SQLite adaptive store parity
items.contract: Add a SQLite-backed adaptive store matching Scrapling default durable storage behavior while preserving the Go Store interface.
ready_when: FileStore compatibility row is complete and Store interface remains stable.
acceptance: Temp-database fixtures prove save/load, domain isolation, reopened persistence, copied loaded fingerprints, close behavior, schema compatibility errors, and use of Scrapling-style storage table fields.
done_signal: TestSQLiteStore passes with temp databases.

items.name: BrowserFetcher interface and chromedp/playwright adapter decision
items.contract: Define a Go browser fetcher contract for dynamic pages, page actions, wait conditions, resource blocking, and response extraction before binding to an engine.
ready_when: Static Response and FetcherSession behavior is validated.
not_ready_when: The row tries to implement stealth, proxy rotation, and browser actions in one slice.
acceptance: A fake browser engine fixture proves the public contract before choosing the real engine dependency.
done_signal: Browser fetcher contract tests pass without launching a real browser.

items.name: Real browser adapter with JavaScript fixture
items.contract: Bind BrowserFetcher to one real Go browser engine and prove dynamic content extraction against a local JavaScript fixture.
ready_when: BrowserFetcher interface row is validated.
acceptance: Local chromedp fixture proves navigation, JavaScript-rendered content, request header forwarding, timeout on missing selector, and Response conversion without live web access.
done_signal: TestBrowserAdapter passes when GOSCRAPLING_CHROME points to a working Chrome/Chromium executable.
The test skips in normal hermetic CI unless GOSCRAPLING_CHROME or GOSCRAPLING_CHROME_AUTO=1 is set.

items.name: Browser fetch markdown dump
items.contract: Add a browser-rendered markdown dump path that turns rendered HTML into compact AI-readable Markdown while preserving headings and links and stripping navigation, script, style, and UI noise by default.
ready_when: BrowserFetcher interface and fake browser engine contract are validated.
A local fixture can exercise rendered HTML without launching a real browser.
not_ready_when: The implementation requires live web access or a real browser process for the core test.
The row expands into CLI flags, MCP tools, or full readability extraction beyond markdown dump behavior.
acceptance: A fake browser engine returns HTML containing headings, links, nav, script, style, and article content.
FetchMarkdown preserves headings and links in deterministic Markdown output.
FetchMarkdown strips script/style content and default navigation noise without live network access.
done_signal: TestBrowserFetchMarkdownDump passes with fake browser-engine HTML fixtures.

items.name: Browser semantic tree extraction
items.contract: Expose a browser-rendered semantic tree for AI agents that summarizes visible elements with stable node IDs, role, accessible name/text, tag name, XPath or selector path, value state, disabled state, and interactivity.
ready_when: Browser markdown or rendered HTML fixture path can provide deterministic HTML to the extractor.
The row remains limited to semantic extraction and does not require browser actions.
not_ready_when: The implementation attempts full accessibility tree parity or CDP backend node integration.
The implementation requires live browser execution for the core test.
acceptance: A local HTML fixture with buttons, links, inputs, labels, disabled controls, and nested content returns a deterministic semantic tree.
Each relevant element includes role, name or text, tag, XPath, interactivity, href, and value/disabled/checked state where applicable.
Noise nodes such as script/style and whitespace-only text are omitted.
done_signal: TestBrowserSemanticTreeExtraction passes with fake browser-engine HTML fixtures.

items.name: Browser sessions and page pool lifecycle
items.contract: Add DynamicSession-style lifecycle with reusable browser contexts/pages, page pool stats, and clean close semantics.
ready_when: Real browser adapter or fake-backed engine seam is stable.
not_ready_when: The row requires a live browser for the core session lifecycle proof.
The row expands into wait actions, downloads, screenshots, XHR capture, context options, resource blocking, stealth, or proxy behavior.
acceptance: Fake engine fixtures prove session default option reuse and page slot reuse without live browser execution.
Concurrent fetch fixtures prove max page bounds, busy/free stats, and queued work starting only after a page is free.
Error and close fixtures prove error page counts, idempotent close behavior, and closed-session rejection.
done_signal: TestBrowserSessionPool and the full Go test suite pass; generated queue docs expose the next assignable browser rows.

items.name: Browser wait conditions, page actions, downloads, screenshots, and XHR capture
items.contract: Port dynamic fetch controls for wait selector/state, network idle, fixed wait, page actions, downloads, screenshots, and captured XHR responses.
ready_when: Browser session pool is stable.
not_ready_when: The row expands into stealth, Cloudflare challenge solving, proxy rotation, live-web browser tests, or Playwright callback APIs not expressible through the Go engine seam.
acceptance: Fake-engine fixtures prove wait selector/state, network idle, fixed wait, page actions, capture_xhr, screenshot options, and binary body/download bytes are passed through the browser engine seam.

BrowserResult conversion attaches screenshot bytes to response metadata and converts captured XHR/fetch BrowserResult values into Response.CapturedXHR entries with headers, status, reason, URL, and body preserved.
Chromedp adapter code executes screenshot capture, regex-matched XHR/fetch collection, and best-effort non-HTML document body preservation without live-web test dependencies.
done_signal: TestBrowserActionsAndCapture and the full Go test suite pass; generated queue docs expose the next assignable browser row.

items.name: Browser context options and resource blocking
items.contract: Support browser context options including cookies, locale, timezone, user agent, extra headers, proxy, CDP/real Chrome selection, resource disabling, custom blocked domains, ad-domain blocking, and DNS-over-HTTPS flag.
ready_when: Browser adapter and session rows are stable.
not_ready_when: The row adds stealth, anti-bot, Cloudflare bypass, proxy rotation, or live-browser-only behavior.
The row requires copying the upstream ad-domain list instead of using a small explicit Go-owned blocklist boundary.
acceptance: Fake engine fixtures prove cookies, locale, timezone, user agent, proxy, CDP URL, real Chrome selection, resource flags, ad blocking flag, DNS-over-HTTPS flag, and extra flags are explicit, validated, defensively copied, and passed through without hidden stealth behavior.
Session fixtures prove browser context defaults merge with per-request options for cookies, locale headers, blocked domains, and ad-block flags.

Chromedp adapter code consumes the explicit request fields for remote allocator, proxy server, headers, cookies, timezone, URL blocking patterns, DNS-over-HTTPS flags, real Chrome executable selection, and extra flags.
done_signal: TestBrowserContextOptions and the full Go test suite pass; generated queue docs expose the next assignable browser rows.

items.name: Stealth browser controls and fingerprint options
items.contract: Expose stealth controls separately from normal browser fetching: deterministic browser-like header generation, Google referer opt-in, WebRTC blocking, canvas-noise script injection, WebGL disabling, extra launch flags, real Chrome selection, and proxy hygiene with unsupported challenge-solving claims rejected visibly.
ready_when: Normal browser context options are stable.
acceptance: Fixtures prove stealth mode is opt-in and copied into BrowserRequest without hidden defaults.
Generated browser-like headers and Google referer are deterministic and preserve caller headers unless GoogleReferer explicitly replaces the referer.
WebRTC, canvas, WebGL, real Chrome, extra flags, and proxy controls are visible to the browser engine or chromedp adapter.
SolveCloudflare returns an operator-visible ErrUnsupportedBrowserChallenge browser option error, and boundaries docs describe supported behavior.
done_signal: TestStealthBrowserControls passes with full repository validation.

items.name: Cloudflare challenge strategy boundary
items.contract: Document and test the Go-owned Cloudflare/Turnstile challenge boundary: challenge solving is disabled by default, SolveCloudflare is an explicit unsupported option that fails before engine work, and any future solver requires deterministic local fixtures plus operator-visible controls before claims ship.
ready_when: Stealth browser controls are explicit and tested.
acceptance: Tests prove normal browser and explicit stealth controls do not enable challenge solving by default.
Tests prove SolveCloudflare returns ErrUnsupportedBrowserChallenge wrapped in ErrBrowserOptions before any browser engine fetch.

Boundary docs and exported CloudflareChallengeBoundary status helper state that Cloudflare/Turnstile solving is unsupported until a future row adds deterministic local fixtures and operator-visible controls.
done_signal: TestCloudflareBoundary passes with full repository validation.

items.name: Spider request, result, scheduler, and session contracts
items.contract: Port Scrapling spider concepts into typed Go request/result/session/scheduler interfaces with deterministic fixture scheduling.
ready_when: FetcherSession is complete and request/response behavior is fixture-backed.
not_ready_when: The row includes robots, cache, checkpoint, sitemap templates, and live crawling in the same slice.
acceptance: A fake fetcher drives deterministic scheduling, callback results, and session reuse.
done_signal: Spider core tests pass using only fake fetchers and local fixtures.

items.name: Crawler engine concurrency, domain limits, and download delay
items.contract: Add the crawler engine loop controls for global concurrency, per-domain concurrency, backpressure, context cancellation, and download delays.
ready_when: Spider core request/result/session/scheduler contracts are validated.
acceptance: Fake sessions prove bounded global active fetches, per-domain active fetch limits, scheduler backpressure, deterministic download delay calls, and context cancellation before fetch.
done_signal: TestSpiderEngineConcurrency passes with fake sessions and no live network access.

items.name: Allowed domains and offsite filtering
items.contract: Add allowed_domains-style filtering and offsite request statistics before live crawling controls are layered on top.
ready_when: Spider core scheduler and stats are stable.
acceptance: Fake requests prove exact-domain and subdomain follow requests are fetched, offsite and suffix-trap requests are dropped, and offsite statistics increment separately from duplicate skips.
done_signal: TestSpiderAllowedDomains passes with fake sessions and no live network access.

items.name: Robots.txt manager and delay directives
items.contract: Port robots.txt compliance with cached parser lookup, can_fetch allow/deny checks, crawl-delay/request-rate delay calculation, start-domain prefetch, per-request SID/user-agent handling, and crawler stats for disallowed requests.
ready_when: Crawler engine filtering hooks are available.
acceptance: Local robots.txt fixtures prove allow/deny precedence, crawl-delay, request-rate, and wildcard user-agent matching without live network calls.
Robots prefetch fetches each seed domain once through the requested SID and later parser reads are served from cache.

Crawler robots mode filters disallowed requests, applies the maximum of configured delay, Crawl-delay, and Request-rate delay, preserves request user-agent matching, and records robots stats without counting filtered URLs as fetched requests.
done_signal: TestRobotsTxtManager passes with full repository validation.

items.name: Development response cache
items.contract: Add spider development cache behavior keyed by request fingerprint with encoded response bodies and cache hit/miss stats.
ready_when: Request fingerprints and Response body helpers are validated.
acceptance: Temp-dir fixtures prove cache put/get/clear, binary-safe bodies, method separation, and cache hit/miss stats.
done_signal: TestSpiderResponseCache passes.

items.name: Checkpoint pause and resume
items.contract: Add JSON checkpoint persistence for scheduler pending requests and seen fingerprints with atomic save, load, cleanup, and context-driven pause/resume hooks.
ready_when: Scheduler fingerprints and crawler loop are stable.
acceptance: Temp-dir fixtures prove checkpoint save/load/cleanup uses an atomic temp-file rename and preserves pending request order plus seen fingerprints.
A paused crawler with CheckpointDir saves pending scheduler state and returns a paused result.
A later crawler run with the same CheckpointDir restores pending requests without replaying completed start requests and cleans up after successful completion.
done_signal: TestSpiderCheckpoint passes with full repository validation.

items.name: Blocked response detection and retry hooks
items.contract: Add Scrapling-style blocked response detection and retry hooks with default blocked status codes, per-request retry counters, retry scheduling, proxy cleanup, and blocked retry stats.
ready_when: Crawler engine loop and stats are stable.
acceptance: Fake crawler sessions prove default blocked status detection retries a request with DontFilter, lower priority, incremented RetryCount, and cleared proxy metadata.
A custom IsBlocked hook can override default detection and a RetryBlockedRequest hook can modify the retry request before scheduling.
MaxBlockedRetries caps blocked retries and stats count blocked responses and scheduled retries.
done_signal: TestSpiderBlockedRetry passes with full repository validation.

items.name: Spider lifecycle hooks, streaming, item hooks, and expanded stats
items.contract: Port spider lifecycle hooks and observability: on_start, on_close, on_error, on_scraped_item, stream output, status counters, response bytes, timing, per-session stats, and ItemList export.
ready_when: Crawler engine loop and result struct are stable.
acceptance: Fake crawl fixtures prove OnStart, OnClose, OnError, and OnScrapedItem lifecycle order with item modification and dropping.
Crawler Stream yields accepted items while preserving the final Result and error channel.
Stats cover failed requests, dropped items, status counters, response bytes, per-domain bytes, per-session counts, timing, and ItemList JSON/JSONL export.
done_signal: TestSpiderLifecycleStatsAndStream passes with full repository validation.

items.name: LinkExtractor and crawl templates
items.contract: Port LinkExtractor plus Go-native CrawlSpider and SitemapSpider template helpers with allow/deny regex filters, domain filters, restrict CSS/XPath scopes, extension filtering, canonicalization/fragment handling, process hooks, sitemap indexes, robots Sitemap directives, and rule dispatch.
ready_when: Response.follow and selector helpers are stable.
acceptance: Local HTML fixtures prove LinkExtractor extraction, dedupe, allow/deny regex, allow/deny domains, restrict CSS/XPath scopes, extension filtering, canonicalization, fragment handling, and process hooks.
CrawlSpider rule fixtures prove generated requests, callbacks, priorities, and process_request mutation.
SitemapSpider fixtures prove sitemap indexes, robots Sitemap directives, sitemap_follow filtering, alternate links, first-matching rule dispatch, and no-live-network request generation.
done_signal: TestSpiderLinkExtractorAndTemplates passes with full repository validation.

items.name: Spider static, dynamic, stealth, and proxy session adapters
items.contract: Connect spider SessionManager to static fetcher sessions, browser sessions, explicit stealth browser sessions, and proxy rotation with SID routing, lazy/eager lifecycle semantics, typed per-request option hooks, response meta merging, and operator-visible proxy/stealth controls.
ready_when: Fetcher, browser session, and proxy rows are complete.
acceptance: Local HTTP fixtures prove StaticSessionAdapter routes GET/POST requests by SID through fetchers.FetcherSession and preserves request headers/body plus response meta.

Fake browser fixtures prove BrowserSessionAdapter and StealthBrowserSessionAdapter route by SID, forward typed browser options, enforce explicit stealth options, and close cleanly through SessionManager.
Local proxy fixtures prove static proxy rotation and browser proxy rotation are explicit operator controls, rotate per request, and surface selected proxy metadata.
done_signal: TestSpiderSessionAdapters passes with full repository validation.

phase-5-cli-tooling.name: Phase 5 - CLI, MCP, and Gormes integration

items.name: CLI static extract GET command
items.contract: Expose a Go `goscrapling extract get` command that fetches local/static pages, applies headers, timeout, redirect mode, optional CSS selection, and writes txt/html output files.
ready_when: Response and static fetcher APIs are stable enough for command output fixtures.
acceptance: Local httptest fixtures prove `extract get` writes selected text, full HTML, request headers, timeout parsing, and parse errors without live network calls.
done_signal: TestCLIExtractGet passes from local fixtures.

items.name: CLI static extract method and request body expansion
items.contract: Extend the static extract command group with POST, PUT, DELETE, form body, JSON body, and query parameter handling while keeping tests local and deterministic.
ready_when: CLI static extract GET command is complete.
acceptance: Local HTTP fixtures prove method routing, body handling, query parameters, and output files without live network calls.
done_signal: Static extract method tests pass from local fixtures.

items.name: Full CLI E2E validation harness
items.contract: Provide a deterministic full binary E2E smoke suite for the static CLI surface and document the optional robots-gated live practice-site suite.
ready_when: Static extract GET and static extract method expansion are complete.
acceptance: Local binary E2E covers GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, selected text output, selected HTML output, headers, query params, JSON body, form body, followed redirects, and held redirects without live network access.
README documents the optional live practice-site command and its robots.txt gating.
Live practice-site E2E fails unless at least five robots-allowed real scrapes complete, including CSS selector extraction, raw document output, and custom header echo coverage.
done_signal: TestGoscraplingFullLocalEndToEnd passes.
The live E2E suite is runnable only with GOSCRAPLING_LIVE_E2E=1 and robots preflight.
TestLivePracticeSitesEndToEnd reports real completed scrape counts for the live feature lanes.

items.name: Cross-layer local E2E validation harness
items.contract: Prove the implemented local layers compose end to end: static fetcher, response selectors, parser adaptive storage, spider flow, CLI binary extraction, and Gormes browser-tool adapter using only hermetic fixtures.
ready_when: Existing layer-specific tests are present and the harness can use local fixtures only.
not_ready_when: The proof requires live web access, credentials, a real browser, stealth behavior, proxy rotation, or unplanned production feature work.
acceptance: A local server fixture is fetched and parsed through public goscrapling APIs.
Adaptive selector save and relocate uses a temp persistent store.
A spider flow follows a local link and emits an item from the detail page.
The complex stateful E2E covers session cookies, basic auth POST, query params, concurrent detail fetching, adaptive relocation, multi-follow spider output, and CLI attribute extraction.
The goscrapling CLI binary writes selected fixture output to disk.
The Gormes browser extraction adapter returns rendered markdown from a fake browser engine.
done_signal: go test ./cmd/goscrapling/e2e/crosslayer -run TestGoscraplingCrossLayerLocalEndToEnd -count=1 passed with hermetic fixtures.
go test ./cmd/goscrapling/e2e/complex -run TestGoscraplingComplexStatefulEndToEnd -count=1 passed with hermetic fixtures.
Full completion gate passed without live network dependencies.

items.name: CLI extract markdown, AI-targeted, and browser modes
items.contract: Add the remaining extract output and fetch modes: markdown conversion, AI-targeted cleanup, dynamic browser fetch, and stealth fetch as explicit, test-backed CLI surfaces.
ready_when: Static extract methods are complete.
Browser fetcher command paths use a stable fake-backed seam for hermetic tests.
not_ready_when: The row would require live browsers, live websites, or untested stealth claims.
acceptance: .md outputs use the shared HTML-to-Markdown renderer instead of plain text.
--ai-targeted sanitizes local HTML fixtures by focusing main/body content, removing hidden/noise nodes, comments, and zero-width characters.
extract fetch and extract stealthy-fetch parse browser flags and forward BrowserOptions through a fake-backed seam without live browser or stealth-bypass claims.
done_signal: TestCLIExtractAdvancedModes passes from local fixtures and fake browser fetchers.

items.name: CLI interactive shell command surface
items.contract: Map Scrapling's interactive shell concepts into a Go command surface with scripted evaluation first, before any full REPL dependency.
ready_when: Static CLI extract behavior is stable.
not_ready_when: The row tries to build a full interactive REPL before scripted command fixtures exist.
acceptance: Scripted shell fixtures prove get(url), print(...), page/response shortcuts, pages history, CSS selector counts, and selected text extraction without live web access.
Binary E2E proves goscrapling shell -c composes get, selectors, page history, and curl2fetcher against local HTTP fixtures.
done_signal: TestCLIShell passes from local httptest fixtures.
TestGoscraplingShellBinaryEndToEnd passes from hermetic binary fixtures.

items.name: Gormes web-search tool adapter
items.contract: Expose goscrapling as a production-friendly Go web search/scraping tool for Gormes without importing Gormes runtime dependencies into the core library.
ready_when: Static fetcher and response objects are validated
Tool input/output schema is designed separately from library APIs
Gormes integration boundary is documented as an adapter, not a core dependency.
not_ready_when: The row tries to replace Gormes web search, browser tools, or channel rendering in one slice
The adapter needs live network access to prove its first behavior.
acceptance: A fake tool call can fetch a local page, extract selected content, and return structured evidence
The adapter output includes URL, title, content, HTTP status, content type, final URL, and selector evidence without depending on goscrapling internals.
done_signal: TestGormesIntegration passes without reaching the network.
The Gormes boundary docs link back to the goscrapling strategy page.

items.name: Gormes browser extraction tools
items.contract: Expose deterministic Gormes-facing browser extraction tool adapters for rendered markdown, links, semantic tree, structured data, and basic form/interactive-element discovery using fake browser engines and tool-call fixtures.
ready_when: Browser markdown and semantic tree rows are validated.
A fake browser engine can return deterministic rendered HTML for adapter tests.
not_ready_when: The row requires live LLM calls, live web access, a real browser, or Gormes runtime changes outside the adapter boundary.
The row attempts a full MCP server implementation instead of Gormes-facing extraction adapters.
acceptance: Fake tool-call fixtures prove rendered markdown, links, semantic tree, structured data, and interactive/form discovery responses.
Tool outputs are deterministic, text-first, and do not require live LLM, live browser, or live network access.
The adapter names and schemas are documented as goscrapling-owned while inspired by Lightpanda MCP tool taxonomy.
done_signal: TestGormesBrowserExtractionTools passes with a fake browser engine.
portfolio-and-gormes-fit.md documents the fake-engine browser adapter boundary.

items.name: MCP scraping tool server
items.contract: Expose a deterministic Go MCP-style scraping tool layer with tool schemas and get, bulk_get, fetch, bulk_fetch, stealthy_fetch, bulk_stealthy_fetch, screenshot, open_session, close_session, and list_sessions handlers backed by injectable static/browser seams, CSS/main-content extraction, session lifecycle, and no live LLM/network requirement for tests.
ready_when: Static CLI extract and fetcher APIs are stable enough for tool output fixtures.
acceptance: Fake static tool calls prove get and bulk_get schemas, CSS selector extraction, main-content extraction, and structured response models without live network.
Fake browser tool calls prove fetch, bulk_fetch, stealthy_fetch, bulk_stealthy_fetch, and screenshot controls without launching a real browser.
Session fixtures prove open_session, list_sessions, close_session, typed session reuse, and error handling without live LLM or MCP transport dependencies.
done_signal: TestMCPServerTools passes with full repository validation.

items.name: Install command, Docker image, and dependency packaging docs
items.contract: Provide a non-mutating Go-native install command that reports goscrapling CLI, browser-runtime, and Docker packaging requirements without silently downloading browsers, plus docs that map the upstream Scrapling install/Docker behavior to this owned boundary.
ready_when: Browser adapter dependency boundary is documented.
The command proof is hermetic and does not invoke package managers, browsers, Docker, or network downloads.
acceptance: goscrapling install and install --help describe installation, browser-runtime, and Docker packaging requirements without performing downloads.
goscrapling install --json returns deterministic structured dependency metadata with browser downloads marked false.
Docs explain the owned divergence from Scrapling install/Playwright behavior and provide local/Docker packaging guidance.
done_signal: TestCLIInstallCommand passes and no test shells out to package managers, browsers, Docker, or network services.
not_ready_when: The slice would install Playwright/Chrome, build or publish containers, or inspect host-specific browser state as required behavior.

items.name: Public docs, examples, and API reference parity
items.contract: Maintain Go docs/examples for parser, adaptive scraping, fetchers, browser fetching, spiders, CLI, MCP, and migration guidance mapped from upstream docs.
ready_when: Core APIs have stable examples for each subsystem.
acceptance: Examples compile for public parser and static fetcher APIs, and README maps parser, adaptive, static fetcher/response, browser, spider, CLI, MCP/Gormes, migration, and excluded docs/assets groups to explicit Go statuses.
done_signal: TestExamples passes with README status-map checks.

items.name: Benchmarks and parity scorecard
items.contract: Add benchmark coverage and a generated parity scorecard so claims such as coverage, speed, and feature completion remain evidence-backed.

items.name: Full upstream app map and py2many static reference
items.contract: Inventory every validator-discovered upstream Scrapling source, test, doc, and docs asset into a generated app-map manifest, link relevant py2many static reference outputs as docs evidence, and avoid claiming generated Go parity when py2many is unavailable.

Every non-excluded entry names a feature anchor, Go target, progress row, conservative coverage status, and translation suitability.
Relevant py2many reference output paths are linked as static evidence and described without claiming generated Go output.
upstream-app-map.md and builder-loop docs are regenerated from source ledgers.
done_signal: App-map validation passes with no unmapped or stale upstream refs.
Generated upstream-app-map.md reflects upstream-app-map.json.
Generated builder-loop docs are regenerated from the updated progress ledger.

items.name: Future upstream release delta and unclassified surfaces
items.contract: Keep a non-builder umbrella for Scrapling features introduced after the observed upstream baseline or source surfaces that a future parity audit finds unclassified.

not_ready_when: This umbrella has not been split into one row per newly discovered feature surface.

acceptance: Future upstream deltas are split into concrete progress rows before any builder work starts.

items.name: Scrapling-shaped Go package taxonomy
items.contract: Move goscrapling runtime code into Go packages that resemble Scrapling source taxonomy while preserving the root package as a compatibility facade for current callers.
ready_when: Current parser, fetcher, response, browser, storage, and spider tests pass in the flat package layout.
The package map preserves current root API entrypoints through type aliases and constructor wrappers.
acceptance: Runtime implementation files are grouped under Scrapling-recognizable Go packages instead of one crowded root package.
The root package re-exports the existing stable public types and constructors used by README, CLI, examples, and spider sessions.
spider runtime code moves to a plural `spiders` package matching upstream taxonomy.
Feature-map and boundary docs describe the package taxonomy and root facade rule.
done_signal: go test ./... -count=1 passes after the package split.
progress validation and JSON validation pass.
git diff --check reports no whitespace errors.

items.name: Shell curl parser helpers and fetcher conversion
items.contract: Port the bounded Scrapling shell curl helpers as scripted, hermetic goscrapling shell behavior: parse DevTools-style curl commands into request metadata and optionally execute them through the static fetcher against local fixtures.
ready_when: The shell remains scripted with -c; no interactive REPL is required.
Curl execution uses httptest/local fixtures only and does not depend on live web requests.
not_ready_when: The implementation would require a full IPython-style REPL, browser fetchers, proxy rotation, or live network access.
acceptance: uncurl scripted shell output exposes method, URL, headers, cookies, params, and body metadata parsed from DevTools-style curl commands.
curl2fetcher scripted shell execution uses the static fetcher against local httptest fixtures and updates page/response/pages shortcuts.
Unsupported curl flags or malformed commands return parse errors without live network side effects.
done_signal: TestCLIShellCurlHelpers passes from local fixtures.

items.name: Shell static method shortcuts beyond get
items.contract: Extend the scripted goscrapling shell shortcuts from get(url) to the remaining upstream static Fetcher methods post, put, and delete with local request-option fixtures.
ready_when: The shell remains scripted with -c; no interactive REPL is required.
Static method shortcut tests use httptest fixtures only.
not_ready_when: The implementation would require browser fetchers, async sessions, full REPL support, or live network access.
acceptance: post, put, and delete scripted shell shortcuts issue the matching HTTP methods to local httptest fixtures.
Request body and header options for method shortcuts are parsed narrowly enough to mirror existing extract command fixtures.
page, response, and pages shortcuts update after each method call.
done_signal: go test ./internal/cli/shell -run TestCLIShellHTTPMethodShortcuts -count=1 passes from local fixtures.

items.name: Shell scripted help and namespace listing
items.contract: Expose a bounded goscrapling shell help() shortcut that mirrors Scrapling's shell banner intent for the scripted Go shell by listing supported shortcuts, page variables, curl helpers, and the no-REPL boundary without touching the network.
ready_when: The shell remains scripted with -c; no interactive REPL is required.
The help fixture asserts command output only and does not fetch any URL.
not_ready_when: The implementation attempts a full interactive REPL, IPython-compatible introspection, browser helpers, or live network examples.
acceptance: help() in shell -c prints the supported scripted shortcuts and variables without requiring a fetched page.
The output lists get, post, put, delete, page, response, pages, uncurl, and curl2fetcher.
The output explicitly says interactive REPL support is not implemented in goscrapling.
done_signal: go test ./internal/cli/shell -run TestCLIShellHelpShortcut -count=1 passes from command-output fixtures.

items.name: Shell pages history expression shortcuts
items.contract: Expose bounded scripted goscrapling shell expressions for inspecting pages history entries so the Go shell covers Scrapling's documented pages[0]/pages[-1] history exploration without implementing a full REPL.
ready_when: The shell remains scripted with -c; no interactive REPL is required.

not_ready_when: The implementation attempts general Python indexing, arbitrary expressions, full REPL support, or live network examples.

pages[index].status returns the selected response status code.
Out-of-range pages indexes return a parse error without panics.

items.name: Shell view command boundary
items.contract: Map Scrapling's shell view(page) helper into a bounded Go-native scripted shell behavior that avoids launching a browser during tests while making the visualization boundary explicit.
ready_when: The shell remains scripted with -c; no interactive REPL is required.
The visualization fixture uses local httptest HTML and no live browser launch.
not_ready_when: The implementation would open a real browser, depend on OS desktop integration, require live network access, or expand into a full REPL visualization system.

view(page) before any fetch returns a parse error without panics or filesystem side effects.

items.name: Shell browser shortcut boundary
items.contract: Expose explicit scripted-shell boundaries for Scrapling's fetch(url) and stealthy_fetch(url) browser shortcuts so goscrapling reports the unsupported shell shortcut without launching a browser or suggesting stealth bypass behavior.

not_ready_when: The implementation would launch a real browser, add stealth behavior, introduce browser session state, or expand shell parsing beyond explicit fetch/stealthy_fetch boundaries.
acceptance: fetch(url) in shell -c returns a parse error that names the unsupported browser shell shortcut and points to goscrapling extract fetch.

Neither boundary path launches a browser, performs network I/O, or updates page history.
